papers.text: A practice room by the river. Thin walls, as requested.
papers.subject: bandstands
papers.note: Other: the Anglers' water, within earshot through thin walls.

papers.text: We will pay for top billing at the Sunday concert. Posters: PUMPKIN, WITH BAND.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Rodney promised us the riverbank. He promised the Anglers too.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: A sign on the river bridge, for the buses: TIPTOE.
papers.subject: signage
papers.note: Other: bus horns at the bridge (style 1 friction).

papers.text: Your face on every jar of Glasshouse jam. Pruella will check each jar.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: A study: is a bus seen through the glasshouse seen, or grown?
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The study asks for a second bus, as a control. Results at harvest.

papers.text: A hat for your portrait. Then one for the frame. Frames feel the cold.
papers.subject: hats

favour.text: The portrait's hat asks to enter the Quiet Competition. It keeps very still.

clippings.sign: PORTRAIT'S HAT WINS QUIET COMPETITION; GOVERNOR BEAMS
clippings.refuse: HAT WITHDRAWN; COMPETITION HELD IN USUAL SILENCE

papers.text: The timetable out of our window. In it: TIMES VARY. HATS DO NOT.
papers.subject: signage
papers.note: Other: the spotters lose the timetable in the window.

papers.text: Give the Circle a minute. They will hand it back unused.
papers.subject: ceremonies
papers.note: Other: the band minds the favour shown to the Circle.

papers.text: An inquiry into glasshouse acoustics. Tomatoes to sit still.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The inquiry asks for another season. The first was mostly band.
papers.note: Other: the band rehearses in the growers' glasshouse for the inquiry.

papers.text: The prize pumpkin's own glasshouse, on the high street. Tomatoes talk.
papers.subject: gardens
papers.note: Set-up of 'A Glasshouse for One' (premise: a Glasshouse Office glasshouse for a single prize pumpkin). Other: the glasshouse stands in front of the Guild's windows.

papers.text: A fern, for your desk. Then a pond for the fern. Then a fountain.
papers.subject: fountains

favour.text: The fern would like to enter the county show. It is nearly a vegetable.

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR ENTERS FERN IN VEGETABLE SHOW; JUDGES POLITE
clippings.refuse: FERN STAYS ON DESK, STILL NEAR NO FOUNTAIN

papers.note: The gift climbs, badly, toward the trade. The favour puts the growers out (a fern on their show bench).

papers.text: Is jam in a window a show entry? A working group is tasting it.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The jam working group asks for more evidence. And some toast.

papers.text: Lend us the hat shop doorway. It sees nine bus stops and one hat.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A portrait in every county hall. I found you seven good sides.
papers.subject: portraits
papers.note: Your portrait in seven halls (owned).

papers.text: The weighing tent, for the Quiet Competition. Nodding by arrangement.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows
papers.note: Other: the growers lose their weighing tent for the competition.

papers.text: An umbrella, just for you. Perhaps say 'rain' more in speeches?
papers.subject: picnic-weather

favour.text: About the umbrella: it would like a seat on the Bandstand Board. It has brought its own.

clippings.sign: UMBRELLA JOINS BANDSTAND BOARD; CONCERTS MOVED INDOORS

papers.text: Open Till's tea room at the bus station. One sip, for the camera.
papers.subject: ceremonies
papers.note: Set-up of 'The Single Sip'. Other: the photographers crowd the spotters' station.

papers.text: We will hire the high street for our notebooks. They reach two lampposts.
papers.subject: buses
papers.note: Other: the high street, in front of the shop windows.

papers.text: Plant reeds by the bandstand. Reeds hear all and repeat nothing.
papers.subject: gardens
papers.note: Other: the band plays to a screen of reeds.

papers.text: A fanfare per show winner, at our cost. Eight bars an onion, four a radish.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows
papers.note: Other: the growers' judging, interrupted by fanfares.

papers.text: Lunch with the growers at the county show? I booked it for eleven.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows
papers.note: Pruella's lunches (owned).

papers.text: A board by the shops of every bus logged. Then one for the footnotes.
papers.subject: signage
papers.note: Other: the boards stand in front of the shop windows.

papers.text: Stand at the stop a minute. I will log you as a rare sighting.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: The spotters' bench for the drum. Sign: RESERVED, DRUM.
papers.subject: buses
papers.note: Other: the spotters lose their bench and stand (the sign says so by leaving them out).

papers.text: An inquiry into nose prints on our windows, each filed by height.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The inquiry asks to call each pane as a witness. They saw it all.

papers.text: We will pay to name the growers' jam the 8:15. Strawberry, slightly late.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: A survey: how far does a cornet carry over water? Ewan moves back each week.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The survey has reached the far bank. It asks for a wider river.
papers.note: Other: the band minds being measured as a nuisance.

papers.text: A spotting step by the glasshouse. Buses look 20 % greener through it.
papers.subject: gardens
papers.note: Other: spotters peering over the growers' glasshouse.

papers.text: Till's Teas would hire the judges' table. Judging resumes after tea.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows
papers.note: A hire, not a sponsorship (mayor-2 owns those).

papers.text: The band's Sunday, for a timetable reading. With an interval.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Glaze the bandstand with the growers' spare panes. Rain applauds.
papers.subject: bandstands
papers.note: Other: the growers give up their spare glasshouse panes.

papers.text: Pose with the band, holding the cymbals. Do not, at any point, use them.
papers.subject: portraits

papers.text: A Guild tent at the county show, so vegetables can window-shop.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows
papers.note: Other: the tent takes room at the growers' show.

papers.text: Lend our show the towpath for a day. Pumpkins have never seen a boat.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows
papers.note: Set-up of 'The Towpath Show'. Other: the Anglers lose their towpath for the day.

papers.text: Turn the bus stop to face our windows. Then the buses. Then the spotters.
papers.subject: buses
papers.note: Other: the spotters can no longer see their buses coming.

papers.text: The band will hire the arcade on Saturdays. Rattled windows get receipts.
papers.subject: paperwork
papers.note: Other: the tuba rattles shop windows (style 1 friction).
